actions.name: delete_by_query
actions.description: Delete Elasticsearch documents matching a query. This destroys data and cannot be undone, so a bounded maxDocs and at least one of query, termFilters, rangeFilters, or timeFilter are required, the index name must be exact, and _all is rejected. That makes it impossible to empty an entire index by accident. The action waits for the deletion to finish, and a large maxDocs can outlast that wait: a timeout does not cancel the deletion, which keeps running on the cluster with no task id to poll, so a retry after a timeout deletes a further batch.

indexName.description: The exact index to delete documents from. Wildcards, comma-separated lists, and _all are rejected.

maxDocs.description: The maximum number of documents this request may delete. Elasticsearch stops once the limit is reached.

items.description: A range filter for numeric, keyword, or date fields.

field.description: The timestamp field to filter on.

gt.description: Match timestamps greater than this ISO 8601 value.

gte.description: Match timestamps greater than or equal to this ISO 8601 value.

lt.description: Match timestamps less than this ISO 8601 value.

lte.description: Match timestamps less than or equal to this ISO 8601 value.

timeFilter.description: A time-based range filter for timestamp fields.

maxDocs.description: The maximum number of documents to copy. All documents are copied when omitted.

opType.description: Whether to overwrite documents that already exist in the destination (index) or skip them as conflicts (create).

conflicts.description: Whether to abort on the first version conflict or keep processing the remaining documents.

requestsPerSecond.description: The throttle applied to the reindex, in requests per second.

inputSchema.description: The input payload for starting an Elasticsearch reindex.

taskId.description: The task identifier to poll with get_task.

sourceIndex.description: The index documents are copied from.

destIndex.description: The index documents are copied into.

outputSchema.description: The submitted Elasticsearch reindex task.

actions.name: update_aliases
actions.description: Atomically add or remove Elasticsearch alias assignments in a single request, which is how an alias is switched between indices without downtime. This action cannot delete an index; use delete_index for that.

type.description: Whether to add or remove the alias assignment.

index.description: The index or index pattern the alias assignment applies to. Patterns are useful when removing an alias from every index behind it.

isWriteIndex.description: Whether this index becomes the write index for the alias. Only used when type is add.

filter.description: A query that restricts the documents visible through the alias. Only used when type is add.

indexRouting.description: The routing value used for indexing through the alias. Only used when type is add.

searchRouting.description: The routing value used for searching through the alias. Only used when type is add.

actions.description: The alias changes to apply atomically.

inputSchema.description: The input payload for updating Elasticsearch aliases.

acknowledged.description: Whether Elasticsearch acknowledged the alias changes.

appliedActions.description: The number of alias changes submitted in the request.

outputSchema.description: The normalized Elasticsearch alias update response.

actions.name: update_index_mappings
actions.description: Add or update field mappings on an existing Elasticsearch index. Existing field types cannot be changed in place, so incompatible changes require a new index and a reindex.

indexName.description: The index whose mappings are updated.

properties.description: The field mappings to add or update, keyed by field name.

dynamic.description: How Elasticsearch should treat fields that are not mapped explicitly.

inputSchema.description: The input payload for updating Elasticsearch index mappings.

indexName.description: The index whose mappings were updated.

acknowledged.description: Whether Elasticsearch acknowledged the mapping update.

outputSchema.description: The normalized Elasticsearch mapping update response.
